children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with a few basics:

1. How many children do you have or are responsible for?

Please share the names of the children you're asking about, and we'll go through the eligibility criteria together.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have a son named Alex who is 17 and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 17 (over 16), I need to ask: Is Alex currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure to be honest. He goes to college, but I don't know if that counts as "approved education" or not. What does that mean exactly?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a good question! College typically does count as approved education for Child Benefit purposes.

To help determine if Alex's college course qualifies, could you tell me:

**What type of course is Alex doing at college?** For example, is it:
- A-levels or similar qualifications
- A full-time course
- A part-time course
- An apprenticeship

This will help me confirm whether it counts as approved education for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm afraid I don't really know the details of what he's studying or what type of course it is. I know he's at college, but I couldn't tell you if it's A-levels or what exactly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's okay - I understand you don't have all the specific details about his course.

Let me ask a different question that might help: **Does Alex have any paid work, and if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

This is important because you would stop getting Child Benefit if a child aged 16 or 17 starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all. He just goes to college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you, that's helpful to know that Alex doesn't work.

Now I need to ask about your own circumstances: **Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** For example, Alex's other parent or another family member?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

One final question: **Are you the person responsible for Alex - meaning, does he live with you and you provide for his day-to-day needs (such as food, clothes, accommodation)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives here with me and I provide for all his needs - food, clothes, everything he needs day-to-day.

**For Alex: INDETERMINATE**

You meet many of the key eligibility criteria:
- ✓ You live in the UK
- ✓ Alex lives with you and you're responsible for him
- ✓ Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- ✓ Alex is not working 24+ hours per week

However, because Alex is 17 (over 16), he needs to be in "approved education or training" for you to continue receiving Child Benefit. While he attends college, I cannot make a definitive determination about your eligibility because you don't have the specific information about his course type (whether it's full-time, what qualifications he's studying for, etc.).

**What I recommend:**

I suggest you find out more details about Alex's college course - for example, whether it's:
- Full-time or part-time
- What qualifications he's working towards (A-levels, BTECs, etc.)

With this information, you could either:
1. Contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly to discuss Alex's specific course
2. Apply for Child Benefit, providing details of his education on the application form

In many cases, standard college courses do count as approved education, so you may well be eligible - you just need to provide those course details when you claim.
